defaults.prerequisites: Build @breakdown-sh/core and @breakdown-sh/cli, pack both, and install their tarballs with the exact YAML dependency in an otherwise empty temporary package.
defaults.action: Invoke the installed breakdown executable against a real temporary project.

rows.requirement: Issue #143: expose breakdown workflow validate --project PATH --json
rows.oracle: Exit 0; stdout is one compact breakdown.cli-output.v1 success document plus LF; stderr is empty.

rows.requirement: Issue #143: expose concise human validation output
rows.oracle: Exit 0; stdout identifies breakdown.yaml and the Node Definition count; stderr is empty.

rows.requirement: Issue #143: preserve structured core validation failures
rows.oracle: Exit 3; stdout is one compact failure document with invalid_workflow and ordered diagnostics; stderr is empty.

rows.requirement: Issue #143: require an explicit non-empty project root
rows.oracle: Missing or empty --project exits 2 with usage on stderr and no stdout.

rows.requirement: Issues #143, #146, and #147: expose only delivered human commands
rows.oracle: A command outside workflow validate, run create, and exact run inspect exits 2 with usage on stderr and no stdout.

rows.requirement: Issue #146: expose breakdown run create --project PATH [--input ID=PATH]... --json
rows.oracle: Exit 0; stdout is one compact breakdown.cli-output.v1 create_run success document plus LF; stderr is empty; the complete Run is visible on disk.

rows.requirement: Issue #146: reject duplicate or malformed --input overrides as CLI usage errors
rows.oracle: Exit 2; stderr contains usage; stdout is empty; no Run is published.

rows.requirement: Issue #147: expose breakdown run inspect --project PATH --run RUN_ID --json
rows.oracle: Exit 0; stdout is one compact breakdown.cli-output.v1 inspect_run success document plus LF; stderr is empty.

rows.requirement: Issue #147: require one exact non-empty --run argument for inspection
rows.oracle: Missing, empty, or duplicate --run exits 2 with usage on stderr and no stdout; no Run is inferred.

rows.requirement: Issue #158: expose exactly the canonical human commands plus help and version metadata
rows.oracle: The three cataloged human commands, --help, and --version succeed as specified; prepare, retry, refresh, finalize, cancel, unlock, Git, publication, and Executor commands are usage failures.

rows.requirement: Issue #158: expose all six core operations through breakdown operate --project PATH
rows.oracle: Each breakdown.operation-request.v1 variant reaches the packaged core and returns the matching operation value and authoritative disk effects without adapter-side core behavior.

rows.requirement: Issue #158: require one strict bounded UTF-8 automation request
rows.oracle: Malformed JSON, invalid UTF-8, missing or unknown fields, wrong variant shapes, unsupported versions, and requests above 2 MiB produce the cataloged structured failure and no partial mutation.

rows.requirement: Issue #158: emit the exact machine stream contract
rows.oracle: Machine success and expected failure write exactly one compact breakdown.cli-output.v1 JSON document plus LF to stdout, keep stderr empty, and remain within the 12 MiB response limit.

rows.requirement: Issue #158: preserve byte fields and deterministic operation values
rows.oracle: Workflow Input bytes and complete predecessor Result bytes use the cataloged base64 fields; decoded values, ordered arrays/maps, diagnostics, and disk effects match the core operation result.

rows.requirement: Issue #158: implement the cataloged human stream presentation
rows.oracle: Human successes use stdout; failures and diagnostics use bounded stderr; terminal controls and active terminal content are escaped; color appears only on a TTY and NO_COLOR disables it.

rows.requirement: Issue #158: preserve the public failure-kind and exit-code catalog
rows.oracle: Success and usage plus invalid, conflict, unsupported, cancelled, resource_limit, io, and internal outcomes use the exact cataloged exit codes without message-text control flow.

rows.requirement: Issue #158: translate process signals to invocation cancellation
rows.oracle: SIGINT and SIGTERM abort the trusted core invocation; pre-commit cancellation publishes nothing, while the core publication critical section retains its settled commit semantics.

rows.requirement: Issue #158: remain independent of Git and inferred project context
rows.oracle: The installed executable succeeds with no Git executable on PATH and never selects a project, Workflow Definition, or Run from cwd, environment, repository, timestamps, or directory order.
